transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Stratus - Head of ML), Marcus Green (Stratus - CTO), Priya Shah (Stratus - PM)

Summary (auto): Demo of Redwood Eval & Quality Monitoring. Focus on prompt-set-driven regressions, automated regression alerts, and A/B dashboards for model comparison. Discussed integration points with Redwood API, Console and Redwood Optimize recommendations.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you fitting us in. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Owen our SE. Quick around the room?
00:12 Lina Torres: Hi, Lina here, Head of ML at Stratus. We run a mixed retrieval+LLM for product recs and support bot.
00:18 Marcus Green: Marcus, CTO. I'm mostly curious about reliability, SLOs and how alerts look in practice.
00:22 Priya Shah: Priya, PM for the support bot and search experiences.
00:26 Owen Patel: Great, happy to walk through the Eval console and run through a mock A/B and regression scenario. We'll show prompt sets, how we surface regressions, and how A/B comparisons look with cohorts.
00:34 Maya Chen: Goal for today is to validate fit for a small pilot — can we detect quality regressions across prompt sets and compare model variants, and what infra/data you need to run it.

01:05 Owen Patel: Ok, jumping into the Redwood Console share — apologies if the screen resolution is off. On the left is the Eval tab, where you create prompt sets. We typically ingest prompt sets from your QA or product team — we can pull from a CSV, or integrate with your repo or S3.
01:28 Priya Shah: CSV or S3 is fine. We already have a canonical prompt bank, about 1.2k examples. We won't send PII — masked.
01:40 Owen Patel: Perfect. You can tag prompts by flow — "recos", "support", "checkout" — and then assign expected outputs or rubrics. The system supports scalar labels, free-text references, and structured scoring.
01:55 Lina Torres: Can we do multiple ground-truths per prompt? We have acceptable variants for natural responses.
02:02 Owen Patel: Yes, you can upload multiple references and set a metric like semantic-similarity threshold or human-annotated score. We also support automated evals like ROUGE/BLEU, embedding cosine, and custom Python-based metrics in a sandbox.
02:20 Marcus Green: How does the regression alerting work — e.g., we push a new model, we want to know if support flow quality drops by X%?
02:30 Owen Patel: Good question. The pipeline computes baseline metrics per prompt set and cohort. When you deploy a new model variant via Redwood API or bring your own endpoint, Eval runs the comparisons automatically and creates a regression if delta exceeds the thresholds you set. You get an alert, with example failing prompts, and can triage in-console.
02:50 Maya Chen: We can tie alerts to channels — Slack, email, and webhook to your incident system. Alerts include sample traces, tokens, and probability scores where applicable.
03:05 Priya Shah: Probability scores as in model logprobs? We don't always have access to that from some vendor APIs.
03:12 Owen Patel: Right — logprobs are best-effort. For hosted Redwood models you get full telemetry; for external endpoints we rely on what the model returns. But even without logprobs we can use similarity metrics and human labels for regression detection.

05:10 Owen Patel: Now A/B comparisons — you define two model variants: e.g., open-model-v1 quantized and an LLM-finetuned-v2. We run them across the prompt set and show per-prompt side-by-side outputs, aggregate metrics, and cohort breakdowns like "by intent" or "by user tier".
05:35 Lina Torres: Cohorting is important — recos behave differently for long-tail SKUs. Can we filter by metadata?
05:42 Owen Patel: Yep, you can attach metadata to prompts (category, user_tier, session_length), and the UI does slicing/dicing. You can also persist slices and schedule periodic re-runs.
06:00 Marcus Green: About scale — if we run 1.2k prompts across two variants and then integrate daily production samples, what infra does Redwood need?
06:12 Owen Patel: For the pilot we typically run benchmarks from Redwood-hosted infra. If you're on Redwood Dedicated or Private, we can run the pipeline in your environment. For hosted, it's per-run cost and we'll estimate tokens. During production you'll probably want continuous sampling: e.g., 5-10k samples/week for monitoring.
06:28 Maya Chen: We'll include a cost estimate in the pilot proposal — token estimate + eval compute.

08:05 Priya Shah: Walk me through a regression alert example — show the UI?
08:12 Owen Patel: Sure. (screen) Here's an alert list — this one shows a 12% drop in semantic-similarity for "support:fallback" prompt set after model roll. Clicking opens sample failures. You can see the expected answer, variant outputs, similarity score, and annotator comments.
08:36 Priya Shah: I see one failing example where the new model hallucinates a return policy. Can we flag that as high severity?
08:44 Owen Patel: Yes, severity is configurable. Also you can mark specific prompts as high-impact for business SLOs, e.g., "checkout-payment-errors" and those have stricter thresholds.
08:58 Lina Torres: Can we attach playbooks to alerts? So ops know whether to rollback or escalate.
09:06 Owen Patel: You can configure a runbook URL and a webhook that triggers an automation (A/B rollback via Redwood routing) if specified thresholds are breached.

12:00 Maya Chen: Quick question from our side — how do you currently evaluate quality in prod?
12:06 Lina Torres: Right now it's ad-hoc: some telemetry, manual QA, and customer reports. We have labeling throughput but not automated comparisons.
12:15 Maya Chen: Ok, good fit. Our Eval can automate that and then hook into Redwood Optimize for suggestions like dynamic quantization or batching to reduce cost while preserving quality.

15:25 Owen Patel: One subtle piece — prompt set versioning. When you update a prompt set, Eval keeps diffs so your baseline is stable. You can choose to rebase baseline metrics or freeze them for regression detection.
15:44 Priya Shah: That helps for AB tests where we tweak prompts.
15:49 Owen Patel: Exactly. We also store model outputs and token-level deltas so you can inspect changes over time.

18:30 Marcus Green: Security — we need SOC 2, SSO, and audit logs. If we do Private deployment, what's different?
18:40 Maya Chen: For Private you get the control plane on your VPC and can integrate KMS/HSM. We provide audit logs, RBAC, and SAML SSO. We'll send the SOC 2 report and architecture diagram as part of the security pack.
18:58 Marcus Green: Good. Data residency — some of our EU customers need EU-only processing.
19:05 Owen Patel: You can pin workloads to region-specific infra and we support region routing for both hosted and dedicated modes.

22:00 Owen Patel: Back to A/B: here's an A/B dashboard sample — lift plots, distribution of scores, per-prompt fail heatmap. You can export the failing set to a CSV and send to annotators, or integrate with your labeling toolchain.
22:25 Lina Torres: Does Redwood support continuous human-in-the-loop review? We want periodic sampling with human labeling for drift detection.
22:33 Owen Patel: Yes, you can set up a sampling policy — rate-limit, stratified by cohort — and route samples to your labeling backend or Redwood-labeled workflows.

26:45 Priya Shah: About integration — what's the simplest flow to start a pilot?
26:52 Maya Chen: 1) You send the prompt set and 200 annotated examples. 2) We run an initial benchmark across 2 variants we agree on. 3) We configure alerts and dashboards for your high-impact flows. 4) Pilot runs 3 weeks with weekly check-ins.
27:08 Marcus Green: Sounds reasonable. For the benchmark, we want to compare open-model-quantized vs our finetuned hosted model. Will that work?
27:16 Owen Patel: Yes — we can call your hosted endpoint or pull from Redwood catalog. If your hosted endpoint has rate limits, we'll throttle.

30:10 Owen Patel: I want to call out the regression alert granularity — you can set thresholds per-prompt, per-set, and per-cohort. Also, you can define action policies: notify, create incident, or auto-revert routing to a fallback model.
30:34 Priya Shah: Auto-revert is interesting. We might want canary percentage gating first.
30:40 Owen Patel: Canary gating is supported — you can say "roll to 10% and monitor 24h before increasing" and Eval will watch for regressions and either continue rollout or hold.

33:55 Lina Torres: Any limits on custom metrics? We may want a custom scoring function that checks for brand voice compliance.
34:03 Owen Patel: You can upload a scoring function (Python) into a sandboxed interpreter — there's resource limits but it's enough for text heuristics. For heavy compute you'd use an external job and ingest results back into Eval.

38:20 Maya Chen: Let's run through a quick mock A/B with two short prompts — Owen, can you trigger a small demo run?
38:27 Owen Patel: Running now — kicking off comparison across two variants for 20 prompts. (waits) Here's side-by-side: variant A tends to be more terse, variant B more verbose and occasionally hallucinated. You can click the heatmap to surface high-delta prompts.
38:54 Priya Shah: I like how the UI surfaces exact token diffs. That's useful for support where a small hallucination can be high-impact.
39:05 Owen Patel: Also note the regression timeline — you can see historical runs and a run-to-run delta.

43:40 Marcus Green: For the pilot success criteria, we propose: 1) detect regressions with >80% precision on a 200-sample validation set, 2) show A/B lift for core recos, and 3) demonstrate alerting + a runbook. Thoughts?
43:55 Maya Chen: That's reasonable. We'll help instrument precision measurement and provide tooling to compute precision/recall on the annotated set.
44:05 Lina Torres: If we can automatically triage top-20 failing prompts each week that's a big win.
44:11 Owen Patel: You can create a weekly report that exports top failures and sends to your Slack channel.

48:00 Priya Shah: Questions about costs: what's the unit for eval runs? tokens or calls?
48:07 Maya Chen: Usually tokens for model execution plus a small compute fee for evaling and storage for results. We'll include concrete estimates in the proposal.
48:18 Marcus Green: Any hidden ops work for us? We want minimal engineering time for pilot.
48:24 Owen Patel: For a hosted pilot, minimal: provide prompt set CSV, sample masked dataset, and a short integration for your hosted endpoint if you want us to call it. If you want private/Dedicated, there's an onboarding effort which we can scope separately.

52:10 Maya Chen: Quick recap and next steps: we'll send the pricing/pilot proposal by Monday Sep 20, Owen will request the sample data and kick off benchmark on Sep 21, and we'll schedule a benchmark run and follow-up check-in week of Sep 22.
52:32 Priya Shah: Sounds good. Also please include the SOC2 and SSO docs in the packet.
52:36 Maya Chen: Will do.

56:40 Owen Patel: Any final quick questions?
56:44 Lina Torres: No, that's it for now. Thanks — the demo helped a lot.
56:49 Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials.
56:55 Meeting end.
